intro_card.title: Fundações do Inglês
intro_card.explanation: Neste bloco você vai praticar a ordem básica das frases em inglês (Sujeito + Verbo + Objeto), os pronomes pessoais (I, you, he, she, it, we, they), o verbo TO BE (am, is, are) e os artigos (a, an, the). Tudo dentro de frases do dia a dia!
examples: I am a student. (Eu sou um estudante.)
She is an engineer. (Ela é uma engenheira.)
They are at the office. (Eles estão no escritório.)

items.grammar_rule: Verbo TO BE: I am, you are, he/she/it is, we/they are

items.hint: is = é/está (usado com he, she, it)
items.grammar_rule: Verbo TO BE: I am, you are, he/she/it is, we/they are

items.hint: are = somos/estamos (usado com we, you, they)
items.grammar_rule: Verbo TO BE: I am, you are, he/she/it is, we/they are

items.hint: an = um/uma (antes de vogal: a, e, i, o, u)
items.grammar_rule: Artigos: a (antes de consoante), an (antes de vogal)

items.content_en: The cat is on the table
items.hint: the = o/a/os/as (artigo definido, único em inglês)
items.grammar_rule: Artigos: the (definido) = o/a/os/as; a/an (indefinido) = um/uma

exercises.correct_answer: The cat is on the table
The cat is on the table

items.grammar_rule: Pronomes: I, you, he, she, it, we, they

items.hint: am not = não estou/não sou (negativa do TO BE)
items.grammar_rule: Negativa do TO BE: sujeito + am/is/are + not
Negativa do TO BE: sujeito + am/is/are + not

items.hint: Perguntas com TO BE: inverte a ordem → Are you...?
items.grammar_rule: Pergunta com TO BE: am/is/are + sujeito + ...?
Pronomes: It é usado para coisas, animais, tempo, clima

items.content_en: The book is in the backpack
items.grammar_rule: Ordem SVO: The book (S) + is (V) + in the backpack (complemento)

exercises.correct_answer: The book is in the backpack
The book is in the backpack

items.content_pt: Nós não somos de São Paulo
items.content_en: We are not from São Paulo
items.grammar_rule: Negativa do TO BE: sujeito + am/is/are + not

exercises.correct_answer: We are not from São Paulo

items.grammar_rule: Perguntas com WH + TO BE: Where/What/Who + is/are + ...?
Perguntas com WH + TO BE: Where/What/Who + is/are + ...?

items.content_pt: Ele não é o professor, ele é um aluno
items.content_en: He is not the teacher, he is a student
items.grammar_rule: Artigos: the (específico/conhecido) vs a/an (genérico/novo)

exercises.correct_answer: He is not the teacher, he is a student

options: He is not the teacher, he is a student
He not is the teacher, he is a student
He is not a teacher, he is the student
He is not teacher, he is student
exercises.correct_answer: He is not the teacher, he is a student

intro_card.title: Hábitos do Dia a Dia
intro_card.explanation: Aqui você vai praticar o Simple Present — o tempo verbal para falar de rotinas, hábitos e verdades gerais. Vai aprender quando usar DO/DOES para perguntas e negativas, e os advérbios de frequência (always, usually, often, sometimes, never). Tudo com frases sobre a vida real!
examples: I wake up at 7 every day. (Eu acordo às 7 todos os dias.)
She doesn't drink coffee. (Ela não bebe café.)
Do you always take the bus? (Você sempre pega o ônibus?)

items.content_en: I wake up at seven o'clock
items.grammar_rule: Simple Present: sujeito + verbo base (I/you/we/they) para hábitos e rotinas

exercises.correct_answer: I wake up at seven o'clock
I wake up at seven o'clock

items.content_pt: Ela trabalha de segunda a sexta
items.content_en: She works from Monday to Friday
items.grammar_rule: Simple Present: he/she/it + verbo com S (works, eats, goes)

exercises.correct_answer: She works from Monday to Friday

items.hint: have lunch = almoçar (não usa eat lunch normalmente)
items.grammar_rule: Simple Present: sujeito + verbo base (I/you/we/they) para hábitos e rotinas

items.hint: always = sempre (vai ANTES do verbo principal)
items.grammar_rule: Advérbios de frequência: always/usually/often/sometimes/never vêm ANTES do verbo

items.hint: never = nunca (já é negativo, não precisa de don't)
items.grammar_rule: Advérbios de frequência: always/usually/often/sometimes/never vêm ANTES do verbo

exercises.incorrect_sentence: I don't never eat fast food

items.grammar_rule: Negativa no Simple Present: he/she/it + doesn't + verbo BASE (sem S!)

items.content_pt: Eu não dirijo para o trabalho
items.grammar_rule: Negativa no Simple Present: I/you/we/they + don't + verbo base

items.content_en: Do you exercise in the morning?
items.grammar_rule: Pergunta no Simple Present: Do + I/you/we/they + verbo base?

exercises.correct_answer: Do you exercise in the morning?
Do you exercise in the morning?

items.content_en: Does he take a shower at night?
items.grammar_rule: Pergunta no Simple Present: Does + he/she/it + verbo BASE (sem S!)?

exercises.incorrect_sentence: Does he takes a shower at night?
exercises.correct_answer: Does he take a shower at night?
Does he take a shower at night?

items.content_pt: Às vezes eu fico até tarde no trabalho
items.content_en: Sometimes I stay late at work
items.hint: sometimes pode ir no início ou antes do verbo
items.grammar_rule: Advérbios de frequência: sometimes é mais flexível na posição

exercises.correct_answer: Sometimes I stay late at work
Sometimes I stay late at work

items.hint: usually = geralmente; on Sundays (com S) = aos domingos
items.grammar_rule: Advérbios de frequência: always/usually/often/sometimes/never vêm ANTES do verbo

items.content_pt: O que você faz depois do trabalho?
items.content_en: What do you do after work?
items.hint: What do you do = O que você faz (rotina)
items.grammar_rule: Perguntas WH no Simple Present: What/Where/When + do/does + sujeito + verbo?

exercises.correct_answer: What do you do after work?
What do you do after work?

items.hint: Where does she...? (does para he/she/it, verbo sem S)
items.grammar_rule: Perguntas WH no Simple Present: What/Where/When + do/does + sujeito + verbo?

items.content_pt: Meu irmão não come carne, ele é vegetariano
items.content_en: My brother doesn't eat meat, he is vegetarian
items.grammar_rule: Simple Present para estados permanentes e hábitos regulares

exercises.correct_answer: My brother doesn't eat meat, he is vegetarian

options: My brother doesn't eat meat, he is vegetarian
My brother don't eat meat, he is vegetarian
My brother doesn't eats meat, he is vegetarian
My brother not eat meat, he is vegetarian
exercises.correct_answer: My brother doesn't eat meat, he is vegetarian

items.content_pt: Com que frequência você vai ao cinema?
items.content_en: How often do you go to the cinema?
items.grammar_rule: How often + do/does + sujeito + verbo? (pergunta sobre frequência)

exercises.correct_answer: How often do you go to the cinema?
How often do you go to the cinema?

intro_card.title: Agora Mesmo — Present Continuous
intro_card.explanation: O Present Continuous (am/is/are + verbo-ing) é usado para falar sobre o que está acontecendo AGORA, neste momento. Também usamos para planos futuros já combinados. A estrutura é: Sujeito + am/is/are + verbo-ING.
examples: I am studying English. (Eu estou estudando inglês.)
She is cooking dinner. (Ela está cozinhando o jantar.)
They are not working today. (Eles não estão trabalhando hoje.)

items.hint: am + verbo-ing = estou fazendo algo agora
items.grammar_rule: Present Continuous: Sujeito + am/is/are + verbo-ING
Present Continuous: he/she/it + is + verbo-ING

items.content_en: We are waiting for the bus
items.grammar_rule: Present Continuous: we/they + are + verbo-ING

exercises.correct_answer: We are waiting for the bus
We are waiting for the bus

items.hint: What are you doing = O que você está fazendo
items.grammar_rule: Pergunta no Present Continuous: What + am/is/are + sujeito + verbo-ING
Negação: Sujeito + am/is/are + NOT + verbo-ING

items.content_pt: As crianças estão brincando no parque
items.content_en: The children are playing in the park
items.grammar_rule: Present Continuous: they/the children + are + verbo-ING

exercises.correct_answer: The children are playing in the park
The children are playing in the park

items.hint: It is raining = Está chovendo (clima usa IT)
items.grammar_rule: Clima no Present Continuous: It + is + verbo-ING

items.content_pt: Eu estou lendo um livro muito bom
items.content_en: I am reading a really good book
items.grammar_rule: Present Continuous: I + am + verbo-ING

exercises.correct_answer: I am reading a really good book
I am reading a really good book

items.grammar_rule: Pergunta: Am/Is/Are + sujeito + verbo-ING
Present Continuous: he/she + is + verbo-ING

items.content_pt: Eles estão se mudando para uma casa nova
items.content_en: They are moving to a new house
items.grammar_rule: Present Continuous: they + are + verbo-ING

exercises.correct_answer: They are moving to a new house
They are moving to a new house

items.content_pt: Eu não estou me sentindo bem
items.hint: not feeling well = não me sentindo bem
items.grammar_rule: Negação: I + am + NOT + verbo-ING
Present Continuous + to + infinitivo
Pergunta: Why + am/is/are + sujeito + verbo-ING

items.hint: planning = planejando (dobra o N: plan → planning)
items.grammar_rule: Present Continuous para planos futuros

intro_card.title: Olhando Para Trás — Simple Past
intro_card.explanation: O Simple Past é usado para ações que começaram e terminaram no passado. Verbos regulares ganham -ED no final (work → worked). Verbos irregulares mudam de forma (go → went, eat → ate). Na negação e pergunta usamos DID + verbo na forma base.
examples: She went to the store. (Ela foi à loja.)
Did you eat breakfast? (Você tomou café da manhã?)

items.grammar_rule: Simple Past regular: verbo + ED
Simple Past irregular: go → went

items.content_pt: Nós comemos pizza ontem à noite
items.grammar_rule: Simple Past irregular: eat → ate

items.hint: did not + verbo base = negação no passado
items.grammar_rule: Negação no Simple Past: did not (didn't) + verbo base
Pergunta no Simple Past: Did + sujeito + verbo base
Simple Past irregular: buy → bought
Simple Past regular: verbo + ED
Simple Past irregular: tell → told

items.hint: woke up = acordei (passado irregular de WAKE UP)
items.grammar_rule: Simple Past irregular: wake → woke

items.hint: did this cost = custou isso (pergunta com DID)
items.grammar_rule: Pergunta: How much + did + sujeito + verbo base
Simple Past regular: verbos terminados em E ganham só D
Simple Past irregular: forget → forgot
Pergunta com What: What + verbo no passado (sem DID quando What é sujeito)

items.content_en: We did not go to the party
items.hint: did not go = não fomos (negação com DID)
items.grammar_rule: Negação: did not + verbo base (não usar went com did)

exercises.correct_answer: We did not go to the party

options: We did not go to the party
We did not went to the party
We not go to the party
We was not go to the party
exercises.correct_answer: We did not go to the party

items.content_en: She was born in São Paulo
items.hint: was born = nasceu (expressão fixa com BE + born)
items.grammar_rule: Expressão fixa: was/were + born (nascer)

exercises.correct_answer: She was born in São Paulo
She was born in São Paulo

items.grammar_rule: Going to: am/is/are + going to + verbo base

items.content_en: She is going to study English.
items.grammar_rule: Going to: sujeito + is/are + going to + verbo

exercises.correct_answer: She is going to study English

items.content_pt: Nós vamos nos mudar mês que vem.
items.content_en: We are going to move next month.
items.grammar_rule: Going to para planos definidos

exercises.correct_answer: We are going to move next month
We are going to move next month

items.grammar_rule: Will: decisões no momento, promessas, ofertas
Will: previsões e opiniões

items.content_pt: Eles não vão vir à festa.
items.content_en: They are not going to come to the party.
items.grammar_rule: Going to negativa: sujeito + am/is/are + not + going to

exercises.correct_answer: They are not going to come to the party

items.grammar_rule: Will negativa: sujeito + will not (won't) + verbo

items.content_en: Are you going to accept the job?
items.hint: Pergunta com going to: Am/Is/Are + sujeito + going to
items.grammar_rule: Going to interrogativa: inversão do verbo to be

exercises.correct_answer: Are you going to accept the job
Are you going to accept the job

items.content_pt: O que você vai fazer no fim de semana?
items.content_en: What are you going to do on the weekend?
items.hint: What + are you going to = O que você vai
items.grammar_rule: Pergunta WH + going to

exercises.correct_answer: What are you going to do on the weekend

items.content_pt: Ela vai ser uma ótima médica.
items.content_en: She will be a great doctor.
items.grammar_rule: Will + be: futuro do verbo to be

exercises.correct_answer: She will be a great doctor

items.grammar_rule: Will para promessas

items.content_pt: Quando você vai começar o curso?
items.content_en: When are you going to start the course?
items.hint: When + are you going to = Quando você vai
items.grammar_rule: Perguntas WH + going to para planos específicos

exercises.correct_answer: When are you going to start the course
When are you going to start the course

items.grammar_rule: Will + advérbios: posição do advérbio antes do verbo principal

items.content_pt: Eu ia te contar, mas esqueci.
items.content_en: I was going to tell you, but I forgot.
items.hint: was going to = ia (plano que não aconteceu)
items.grammar_rule: Was/were going to: planos passados não realizados

exercises.correct_answer: I was going to tell you, but I forgot

items.content_pt: Não se preocupe, tudo vai ficar bem.
items.content_en: Don't worry, everything will be fine.
items.hint: Don't worry = não se preocupe; will be fine = vai ficar bem
items.grammar_rule: Will para previsões confiantes e encorajamento

exercises.correct_answer: Don't worry, everything will be fine
Don't worry everything will be fine

items.grammar_rule: Adjetivo após verbo to be: sujeito + is/are + adjetivo
Adjetivos em inglês não mudam com gênero/número

items.content_pt: Ele é mais alto que eu.
items.hint: taller = mais alto (-er para adjetivos curtos)
items.grammar_rule: Comparativo curto: adjetivo + ER + than
Comparativo longo: more + adjetivo (3+ sílabas)

items.content_pt: Ela é a mais inteligente da turma.
items.content_en: She is the smartest in the class.
items.grammar_rule: Superlativo curto: the + adjetivo + EST

exercises.correct_answer: She is the smartest in the class

items.content_pt: É o filme mais bonito que eu já vi.
items.content_en: It's the most beautiful movie I've ever seen.
items.grammar_rule: Superlativo longo: the most + adjetivo

exercises.correct_answer: It's the most beautiful movie I've ever seen

items.grammar_rule: Adjetivo descreve estado: sujeito + is + adjetivo

items.content_pt: Hoje está mais quente que ontem.
items.hint: hot → hotter (dobra a consoante final + er)
items.grammar_rule: Comparativo: consoante curta dobra (big→bigger, hot→hotter)

items.content_pt: Ele é tão rápido quanto ela.
items.content_en: He is as fast as her.
items.grammar_rule: Comparativo de igualdade: as + adjetivo + as

exercises.correct_answer: He is as fast as her

items.content_pt: Ela não é tão alta quanto o irmão.
items.content_en: She isn't as tall as her brother.
items.grammar_rule: Igualdade negativa: not as + adjetivo + as

exercises.correct_answer: She isn't as tall as her brother
She isn't as tall as her brother

items.content_pt: Este é o melhor restaurante da cidade.
items.content_en: This is the best restaurant in the city.
items.grammar_rule: Superlativo irregular: good → better → best

exercises.correct_answer: This is the best restaurant in the city

items.grammar_rule: Comparativo irregular: bad → worse → worst

items.content_pt: Quanto mais eu estudo, melhor eu fico.
items.content_en: The more I study, the better I get.
items.grammar_rule: Comparativo duplo: the + comparativo, the + comparativo

exercises.correct_answer: The more I study, the better I get

items.content_pt: Ele é muito mais velho que parece.
items.content_en: He is much older than he looks.
items.grammar_rule: Intensificadores: much/far/a lot + comparativo

exercises.correct_answer: He is much older than he looks

items.content_pt: Essa foi a pior decisão que eu já tomei.
items.content_en: That was the worst decision I've ever made.
items.grammar_rule: Superlativo irregular: bad → worse → worst

exercises.correct_answer: That was the worst decision I've ever made

items.grammar_rule: Possessive adjectives: my, your, his, her, its, our, their
Possessive pronouns: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs
His = dele (adjetivo possessivo masculino)
Our = nosso/nossa (adjetivo possessivo)
Mine vs my: mine substitui 'my + substantivo'

items.content_pt: A casa do João é bonita.
items.grammar_rule: Possessive 's: nome + 's + substantivo
Plurais irregulares: children's, people's, men's
Whose: pergunta sobre posse (não confundir com who's = who is)

items.content_pt: Esses são os seus, não os meus.
items.grammar_rule: Pronomes possessivos em contraste: yours vs mine

items.content_pt: A ideia dela era melhor que a nossa.
items.content_en: Her idea was better than ours.
items.grammar_rule: Ours = o nosso/a nossa (substitui our + substantivo)

exercises.correct_answer: Her idea was better than ours

items.content_pt: O escritório do meu pai fica longe.
items.content_en: My father's office is far away.
items.grammar_rule: Possessive 's com relação familiar

exercises.correct_answer: My father's office is far away

items.content_pt: O carro dos vizinhos é novo.
items.hint: neighbors' = dos vizinhos (plural regular: só apóstrofo)
items.grammar_rule: Plural regular + posse: s' (só apóstrofo após o s do plural)

items.content_pt: Um amigo meu mora em Londres.
items.content_en: A friend of mine lives in London.
items.hint: a friend of mine = um amigo meu (dupla posse)
items.grammar_rule: Double possessive: a/an + noun + of + possessive pronoun

exercises.correct_answer: A friend of mine lives in London

items.content_pt: Esse não é o problema deles.
items.grammar_rule: Their vs they're vs there: their = possessivo

items.hint: Whose + substantivo + are these = de quem são
items.grammar_rule: Whose em perguntas com plural
